case_title: MOHD. AYUB DAR v. STATE OF J & K
previous_criminal_record: Yes, involved in other terrorist cases
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.1208 r/w s.3(3) of TADA Act
confession: Yes, voluntary and truthful confession relied on
aggravating_circumstances: Conspiracy to commit terrorist act, use of firearms, planning and execution of murder
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under TADA Act and IPC s.302, sentenced to life imprisonment and fine
neutral_facts: The accused, along with four other individuals, were charged with the murder of Mirwaiz Moulvi Farooq. The prosecution alleged that the accused were members of a militant group and conspired to eliminate the victim, who was perceived as a political leader and an agent of the Indian government. On the day of the incident, the accused entered the victim's office, where one of them fired at the victim, while the others provided cover. The victim was severely injured and later died from gunshot wounds. The accused's confessional statement, recorded under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, was considered reliable and corroborated by other evidence. The accused was arrested in Delhi in a separate case and later in the instant case. The trial court convicted the accused under the TADA Act and IPC s.302, sentencing him to life imprisonment and a fine. The accused claimed the confession was not made, but the court found it voluntary and truthful.
